answer: Reputation-weighted escrow draw. Each identity must post a timber deposit that scales with its transaction volume; payouts release only after a counterparty confirms delivery. A clone farm pays this deposit per identity but earns reputation too slowly to offset it, so marginal clones run negative. The haven against farming is a hard cap: an identity's escrow ceiling grows only through confirmed volume. Attacker cost is the full deposit per clone, forfeited on any failed confirmation, plus an ivory-tier audit fee triggered above a volume threshold.
